title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to consume enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. In this article, we'll introduce three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in under 30 minutes.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Spinach Bowl with Lemon
* 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
* 100g steamed spinach (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while spinach and lemon provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, cook the chicken to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) and wash the spinach thoroughly.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry Bowl with Bell Pepper
* 100g beef stir-fry (iron: 2.5mg)
* 100g steamed broccoli (iron: 1.5mg, vitamin C: 40mg)
* 1 bell pepper (vitamin C: 100mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Beef stir-fry is a good source of heme iron, while broccoli and bell pepper provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, cook the beef to an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) and wash the broccoli thoroughly.

## Recipe 3: Vegetarian Red Bean and Vegetable Bowl with Lemon
* 100g cooked red beans (iron: 3.5mg, folate: 100mcg)
* 100g steamed vegetables (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Red beans are an excellent source of non-heme iron, while vegetables and lemon provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, cook the red beans to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) and wash the vegetables thoroughly.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's crucial to ensure food safety. Avoid consuming:
* Raw or undercooked meat
* Unwashed or raw vegetables
* Unwashed or raw fruits
* Expired or spoiled food

Please visit our [meal planner](/planner) for more recipes rich in iron and folate.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide a rich source of iron and folate, essential for the health of both mother and baby. Remember to follow food safety guidelines and visit our [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/pregnancy-nutrition) for more information.
